skill.name: format-standardize
skill.description: Standardize formatting and apply consistent style to code, documentation, and generated deliverables using user or project conventions.
skill.summary: Standardizes code, documentation, and content formatting against user or project style rules.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

content.value_statement: Generated work often mixes styles, spacing, and structure. This skill applies consistent formatting so deliverables are easier to review and reuse.
actual_capabilities: Reviews generated deliverables for formatting consistency.
Loads project formatting standards through StandardsRepository when available.
Applies code style checks for indentation, naming, spacing, imports, and line length.
Standardizes documentation headings, lists, code blocks, links, and tables.
Returns standards used, changes made, the formatted deliverable, and validation notes.
limitations: Does not provide a full formatter implementation.
Depends on available project standards or clear user instructions.
Does not verify that code behavior remains correct after broader edits.
Does not include automated tests or formatter integrations itself.

use_cases.title: Prepare Code For Review
use_cases.description: Normalize indentation, spacing, names, imports, and semicolons before a reviewer checks the change.

use_cases.title: Polish Technical Documentation
use_cases.description: Standardize headings, lists, code blocks, links, and tables before publishing a guide or specification.

use_cases.title: Unify Generated Deliverables
use_cases.description: Apply one style across mixed AI-generated code, explanations, validation notes, and examples.

prompt_templates.title: Format A Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single deliverable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Standardize this deliverable for consistent headings, spacing, lists, and punctuation. Preserve the meaning and return the polished version.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Style Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Use known formatter preferences or a style guide.
prompt_templates.prompt: Format this work using our project standards. Use two-space indentation, consistent Markdown headers, sorted imports, and concise validation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Mixed Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Clean up code, documentation, and explanation together.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this mixed deliverable. Standardize the code, documentation, examples, and change summary while keeping the original behavior intact.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release-Ready Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a final formatting pass for release. Report standards used, changes made, the final deliverable, and any remaining formatting risks.

output_examples.input: A React component has extra spaces, mixed semicolon usage, and uneven indentation.
output_examples.output: The component is returned with consistent spacing, indentation, brace style, and semicolon usage, followed by a concise change summary.

output_examples.input: A Markdown guide uses uneven heading levels, mixed bullet styles, and inconsistent code block labels.
output_examples.output: The guide is returned with a clean heading hierarchy, consistent lists, labeled examples, and a short validation section.

output_examples.input: A generated deliverable includes code, explanatory notes, and a final checklist in different styles.
output_examples.output: The deliverable is returned in one consistent structure with aligned terminology, formatting choices, and review-ready validation notes.

best_practices: Provide the style guide or formatter preference before using the skill.
Ask the skill to preserve behavior while changing formatting only.
Review final output for domain accuracy after formatting.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for risky logic refactors instead of formatting cleanup.
Running the skill without specifying important project style constraints.
Treating visual polish as a substitute for tests or expert review.

faq.question: What does this skill standardize?
faq.answer: It standardizes code, documentation, content structure, formatting summaries, and validation notes.

faq.question: Can it use my existing style guide?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed to load project standards when they are available.

faq.question: Does it run external formatting tools?
faq.answer: The skill recommends using tools such as Prettier or linters when specified, but it does not include executable tool code.

faq.question: Will it change code behavior?
faq.answer: It should focus on formatting and presentation. You should review behavior separately after any code changes.

faq.question: Is it useful for Markdown documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks heading hierarchy, lists, spacing, code blocks, links, tables, punctuation, and section consistency.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
